description: Read the accessibility tree: the windows, buttons, text fields and other elements of the applications, with ids (a1, a2, ... for the desktop; w1, w2, ... for a web page), names, states, positions and the actions they offer. An id is only valid for the generation the tree reports: read the tree again after the screen has changed.

query.description: Only elements whose role, name, description or value contain this text.

reason.description: A short note on why you do this; the user sees it.

scope.description: What to read: the window that has the focus (default), every window of the desktop, or the page in the browser.

name: read_accessibility_tree

description: Click an element by its id: from the accessibility tree (a...), from the browser's tree (w...) or from the recognized screen text (o...). Prefer this to clicking at coordinates. A stale id is refused: read the tree again.

id.description: The element's id, for example a17, w3 or o12.

reason.description: A short note on why you do this; the user sees it.

name: click_element

description: Run a shell command in the virtual machine as the user cs (bash -lc). Prefer this to the mouse and keyboard when a task can be done from the command line. The output comes back as text; some commands need the user's confirmation and some are refused.

cwd.description: The directory to run in; the home directory by default.

reason.description: A short note on why you do this; the user sees it.

stdin.description: Text given to the command on its standard input.

timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait before the command is stopped.

name: exec

description: Move the mouse or press its buttons at a point of the screenshot you were given (pixels of that image, origin at the top left). Prefer click_element when the target has an id.

op.description: What to do; drag presses at x, y, moves to to_x, to_y and releases.

reason.description: A short note on why you do this; the user sees it.

to_x.description: Where a drag ends: horizontal position.

to_y.description: Where a drag ends: vertical position.

name: mouse

description: Press one key or one key combination, such as Return, Escape, ctrl+l or alt+F4 (xdotool names). One combination for each call; use type_text for text.

keys.description: The key or combination, with + between the keys.

reason.description: A short note on why you do this; the user sees it.

repeat.description: How many times to press it.

name: key

description: Type text into the element that has the keyboard focus, as a person would at the keyboard. Any Unicode text; a newline presses Enter and a tab presses Tab.

reason.description: A short note on why you do this; the user sees it.

name: type_text

description: Wait inside the virtual machine until something happens, without spending turns: some seconds pass, the screen changes or goes quiet, a text appears on the screen, a window title contains a text, or an element with a given name appears. It answers when the time is up as well.

condition.description: What to wait for: seconds waits the whole time; screen_change until anything on the screen changes; screen_idle until it has not changed for a second; text_visible, window_title and element need a value.

reason.description: A short note on why you do this; the user sees it.

value.description: The text to look for on the screen, in a window title, or in the name of an element.

name: wait_for

description: Ask the user a question and wait for the answer in the chat. Use it when the task is unclear, when something you need is missing, or after an action was rejected and you cannot see how to go on.

reason.description: A short note on why you do this; the user sees it.

name: ask_user

description: End the task: say whether it succeeded and give the user a short summary of what was done or why it was not.

reason.description: A short note on why you do this; the user sees it.

summary.description: What was done, or why it could not be.

name: done
